name: Вимушені розміни
description:
When you calculate variations, you always have to consider all possible captures. Exchanging pieces is also a forcing combination. Your opponent is required to recapture in order to avoid material loss.

What do you have to do?
Win material by a forced exchange.

examples.pgn: 1. Nxf6+ Qxf6 {[%cal Gb2f6]} 2. f4 Qe7 3. fxe5 1-0
examples.text: By exchanging on f6 the black queen ends up on an unfavorable square. White then exploits the pin by advancing the f-pawn. White wins material!

examples.pgn: 1... Rxd1+ 2. Bxd1 Rc1 {[%cal Gc1g1]} 3. Kg2 Rxd1 0-1
examples.text: The bottom rank is vulnerable for white. By exchanging on d1, White can set up a pin that wins a decisive amount of material.

examples.pgn: 1. Nxe7+ Rxe7 {[%csl Re7,Rf8]} 2. Bd6 Rd7 3. Bxf8 1-0
examples.text: This time White can win material with a skewer by first capturing on e7.

examples.pgn: 1. Bxc8 Rxc8 {[%csl Rc8,Rg8]} 2. Ne7+ Kf8 3. Nxc8 1-0
examples.text: We generally don't give up a nice bishop for a knight, but this is an exception! After White captures the knight, White can win with a fork.
